summary: Browser-route restoration requires the owned safe authentication audit event constants. UI copy remains deferred to the dedicated UI stage; its source assertion is therefore deferred with it.
current_flow: The hosted route implementation now composes the durable repository and Stage 2 boundary. Its only additional dependency is the safe runtime auth-event vocabulary; browser UI remains intentionally outside this backend stage.

criteria_map.Generic OIDC validates discovery issuer,: oidc-adapter.ts is the sole discovery/token/JWKS/claim-validation owner using the existing constrained transport.
criteria_map.Public local and hosted auth routes cons: browser-auth.ts composes established local and browser-boundary helpers without converting sessions into Bearer credentials.
criteria_map.Hosted identity is keyed by issuer plus: browser-auth.ts uses durable repository identity, grant, invitation, session, and transaction methods established in Stage 1.
criteria_map.Only the full Control profile mounts UI: index.ts and ui-static.ts restrict UI/browser-auth mounting to the full Control profile.

rounds.question: Should authentication event names be improvised per route?
options: Use the central runtime event vocabulary
rounds.chosen: Use the central runtime event vocabulary

rounds.question: Should Stage 3 pull UI pages forward solely for a static source assertion?
options: Move the UI stage into backend work

citations.finding: Authentication audit records must be safe and browser auth remains separate from the UI implementation layer.
